newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIA keeps foreign share limit unchanged.
newsitem.headline: SIA keeps foreign share limit unchanged.

text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd SIA) will maintain the proportion of its shares that foreign holders can hold at the present 27.5 percent, the Straits Times said on Sunday.
SIA chairman S. Dhanabalan made the announcement at the company's annual general meeting on Saturday, the daily newspaper said.

Dhanabalan's announcement was in response to some shareholders' requests that the foreign shareholding limit be raised in order boost demand for local shares, narrowing the price difference between SIA Foreign shares and Local shares.
SIA shares are traded on the Singapore Stock Exchange in separate local and foreign tranches.
Singaporeans can buy both types, although foreigners are restricted to the foreign tranche.
But greater demand from foreign investors have kept SIA's foreign share prices trading at a premium over local ones.
SIA Local shares closed on Friday at S$7.50, while SIA foreign shares ended at S$13.50.

Dhanabalan said that although raising the foreigners' proportion may reduce the foreign share prices in the short term, fundamentally stronger demand from foreign investors will eventually widen the price gap.
The company was also considering starting a share buy-back scheme, whereby a company uses its own money to buy back its shares, typically improving the company's performance, Dhanabalan said.
But this is still illegal in Singapore and would require adjustments to the laws in the state, he added.
